title: CLCON/322/2015 of Dinesh Chandra Singh Vs Vijay Kumar Dhaundiyal

paras.text:
CLCON No. 322 of 2015
U. C. Dhyani, J.
Mr. B.M. Pingal, Advocate alongwith Mr.
Amar Shukla, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Mr. A.K. Joshi, Additional C.S.C. for the State.
 By means of present contempt petition, the
petitioner seeks to call upon the respondent-contemnor
for non compliance of order dated 31.03.2006 passed
by writ court in writ petition no. 4796 of 2001 (S/S)
which as modified by judgment and order dated
14.09.2010 passed by the Division Bench of this
Hon'ble Court in special appeal no. 24 of 2007 and
further to direct the respondents to comply with the
above orders passed by this Court.
 In writ petition no. 4796 of 2001 (S/S) titled as
Uttaranchal Sangrah Kurk Amin Parishad and another
vs. State of Uttaranchal and others, an order was
passed by learned Single Judge, which is as follows:
"Looking to the grievance of the petitioner, a writ
of mandamus is issued to the opposite parties to
implement the order in its true spirit by according
full status of holder of civil post with all
consequential benefits w.e.f. 16.11.1985 like the
Govt. Servants in view of the aforesaid
judgment".
The order passed by learned Single Judge was
challenged by State of Uttarakhand and others before
the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court in special
appeal no. 24 of 2007, the operative portion of which
is as follows:
"We, accordingly, conclude the matter and, as
such, refuse to interfere with the judgment and
order under appeal, except to the effect that the
consequential benefits which the members of the
petitioner can have pursuant to the siad judgment
and order, will be from 9th November, 2000 and
not w.e.f. 16th November, 1985, as had been
directed by the judgment and order under appeal.
The appeal is, accordingly, disposed of.".

Again the State of Uttarakhand filed special
leave petition before the Hon'ble Apex Court, which
was dismissed on 18.02.2011(Annexure no. 3).
 It is the submission of learned counsel for the
petitioner that whereas 86 plus 44 Sangrah Kurk Amin
Parishad in cooperative department have been granted
benefit of the orders of the Court, the petitioner only
has been left alone. Petitioner is also a member of
Uttaranchal Sangrah Kurk Amin Parishad. It is the
submission of learned counsel for the petitioner that
the order akin to 16th April, 2011 requires to be passed
by the Government in respect of petitioner also.
 Learned counsel for the petitioner confined his
prayer only to the extent that the respondent be
directed to consider the representation of the
respondent by a reasoned and speaking order, in
accordance with law.
 Learned Additional C.S.C. submitted that if
such a direction is issued by the Hon'ble Court, the
same shall be complied with by the respondent.
 Since one of the object of contempt jurisdiction
is to enforce and ensure the compliance of the orders
of the Courts, therefore, contempt petition is disposed
of by directing the respondent to decide the
representation of the petitioner by a reasoned and
speaking order, in accordance with law, in the light of
the judgments of the courts, a brief reference which
has been given in the foregoing paragraphs of this
judgment, at an earliest possible but not later than six
weeks from the date of production of the certified copy
of this order alongwith a copy of representation
enclosing various orders of the Court.
 (U. C. Dhyani, J.)
 17.11.2015 SH
